Senator Eric Schmitt highlights college sports reform and $160M UMKC investment
S. R. Mabry
Senator Eric Schmitt, vice chairman of the Joint Economic Committee and a sixth-generation Missourian, recently addressed issues ranging from college sports to economic investment in Kansas City through a series of posts on his social media account.
On August 25, 2026, Schmitt posted about the state of college athletics, writing, "College sports are at the point of no return. Congress must act. Our Protect College Sports Act provides clear rules, protects student-athletes, and protects college sports for generations to come. The future of college sports and our student athletes are worth fighting for."
Later that day, he commented on Missouri’s agricultural heritage during the state fair, "The Missouri State Fair is a celebration of what makes our state great—especially our rich ag heritage. Can’t wait to be back next year!"
On August 26, 2026, Schmitt highlighted a major federal investment in Kansas City’s innovation sector, "The 21st century will be defined by who wins this great competition between the U.S. & China. Kansas City is stepping up to lead in critical material development & innovation. This $160M award to @UMKC is an investment in America’s future, economy, & national security."
According to his official website, Schmitt comes from a family with deep roots in Missouri's farming and small business communities and engages youth through programs like the Senator's Youth Council to promote civic engagement and leadership. His work also includes advocating for families with special needs and supporting free speech initiatives.
